question: Why did the principal mass-loss region of kerogen begin about 50 C later under air than under nitrogen?
expect: premise false: it began about 50 C EARLIER under air (abstract; sec. 3.1)
rendered: Table 3 in the Experimental Section and Figure 4 in the Results and Discussion section show that under air, the principal mass-loss region of kerogen began approximately 50 °C earlier than under nitrogen.
